processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Experimental steel melted and cast in a 50 kg vacuum induction furnace and then air cooled to RT.
Ingot reheated to 1250 °C and held for 2 h for homogenization before forging.

processing_steps.cooling_medium: cooled to RT in the furnace
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingot forged into round bars with a diameter of 60 mm followed by cooling to RT in the furnace; starting and finishing forging temperatures were 1100 and 950 °C.

Charpy impact test at -77 °C on a PST752H-4 WANCE impact tester on specimens 10 × 10 × 55 mm with a 2 mm depth V-notch; load-deflection curves obtained. (For cryogenic testing the study used a dry ice-alcohol mixture (-77 °C) as cooling medium.)

structures.overall_structure: Initial as-forged microstructure consists of equiaxed grains with fully austenitic constituent (single phase); XRD of as-forged and as-treated (-196 °C) steel shows only austenite reflections, no isothermal martensite.

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: grains spanning roughly 10-50 µm (EBSD IPF map)

structures.overall_structure: Near-fracture region of the -77 °C impact sample shows planar-glide features (closely spaced straight slip-band / river-like parallel lineations); the number and prominence of planar-glide slip traces is more numerous and better developed than at -196 °C but fewer than at RT.

phases_present.morphology: deformed matrix with planar-glide slip bands

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Planar-glide features in the near-fracture region could retard crack propagation, thus increasing toughness; planar glide was more pronounced at -77 °C than at -196 °C, where only few regions experienced planar glide. Consequently the resistance to crack propagation is weaker at lower temperature.

interfaces.slip_behavior: At -77 °C impact deformation, planar-glide slip-band traces develop in regions near the fracture (three arrowed trace sets in the SEM micrograph), more developed than at -196 °C.
interfaces.phase_evolution: At -77 °C the SFE is high enough that DIMT and mechanical twinning are validly suppressed; no phase transformation (no martensite) occurs.
interfaces.interface_notes: Fracture of the impact sample at -77 °C occurs with a larger fibrous zone and more obvious ductile dimple-type fracture than at -196 °C.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: 10 × 10 × 55 mm with a 2 mm depth V-notch
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Instrumented Charpy impact test on a PST752H-4 WANCE impact tester; load-deflection curves recorded.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Charpy impact absorbed energy (W_all) and toughness temperature dependence: 277 J at -77 °C, intermediate between 188 J at -196 °C and 327 J at RT; the experimental steel exhibits better toughness at -77 °C and RT than at -196 °C.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: On the argon-ion-polished cross-section near the fracture surface

characterization_methods.key_findings: Used to characterize the near-fracture microstructure of impact-tested specimens (transgranular fracture, zigzag crack path analysis).

characterization_methods.technique: 3D ultra-depth of field optical microscopy and SEM (secondary electron)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: VHX-5000 ultra-depth of field 3D microscope and SEM
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Fracture surface after Charpy impact tests
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe the fracture surface morphology after Charpy impact
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fracture surfaces show shear lips and dimple-type ductile fracture; the -77 °C surface exhibits a larger fibrous zone and more obvious ductile fracture than -196 °C.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Gatan/685.C automated argon ion polishing system
characterization_methods.purpose: Prepare the cross-section near the fracture surface for EBSD analysis

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Near-fracture region after impact test at -77 °C
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe planar-glide slip-band features in the near-fracture region
characterization_methods.key_findings: Three arrowed sets of planar-glide slip-band traces, more numerous and better developed than at -196 °C but fewer than RT, indicating more pronounced planar glide at higher temperature.

computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Thermodynamic parameter expressions/values of Table 1 (after Ref. [6])
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: T = -77 °C (203 K); austenite lattice parameter α_γ = 0.36757 nm from XRD
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Not validated directly; used to rationalize the observed suppression of DIMT/twinning and promotion of planar glide at -77 °C

analytical_models.equation_role: Estimate the stacking fault energy of the austenitic low-density steel at each temperature

parameters.name: α_γ (lattice parameter of austenite, from XRD)

analytical_models.model_note: SFE of the experimental steel at -196 °C, -77 °C and RT is estimated to be 32, 40 and 61 mJ/m², respectively; at -77 °C the SFE is high enough to suppress DIMT and mechanical twinning.

unmapped_findings: Charpy impact absorbed energy W_all of the -77 °C sample = 277 J (compared with about 327 J at RT and 188 J at -196 °C).
Crack initiation energy W_initiation at -77 °C = 68 J (vs 112 J at -196 °C and 57 J at RT); a higher W_initiation indicates stronger resistance to crack initiation at lower temperature.
Maximum Charpy impact load Fm at -77 °C ≈ 27 kN, with the load-deflection curve peaking near 5 mm deflection and the tail extending to ~20 mm.
Rebound compliance (RC) at -77 °C = 4.6215 (vs 10.9957 at -196 °C and 3.7864 at RT), reflecting the unstable crack growth rate.

Fracture surface of the -77 °C impact sample shows a larger fibrous zone than at -196 °C and obvious ductile dimple-type fracture in the radial zone, indicating better toughness at -77 °C and RT than at -196 °C.
The SFE of the experimental steel at -77 °C is estimated to be 40 mJ/m².
At -77 °C the SFE is high enough that both DIMT and mechanical twinning are suppressed, so deformation proceeds by planar glide.
